summary: The study presents a low-temperature thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for silicon dioxide (SiO2) using 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES), water, and ozone as precursors. The process achieves uniform and perfect surface coverage, even in nanoscale pores, and demonstrates high-quality SiO2 with properties comparable to thermal oxide. Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) at 1000 °C significantly improves certain properties, such as etch rate and oxide charges. The material shows excellent optical, structural, and electrical properties, making it suitable for nanoelectronics and nanotechnology applications.
